key_insight: Large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) can often predict viewpoint rotation using linguistic priors alone; interpretability analyses show that they encode rotation-related transformations in identifiable attention patterns and neuron groups even without visual input.
problem_solved: Determines whether and how text-only inputs suffice for spatial/viewpoint reasoning, and clarifies the internal mechanisms by which LLMs and VLMs perform viewpoint-rotation tasks when visual signals are removed.
method: Design text-only viewpoint-rotation tasks that describe scenes and ask for rotated perspectives (egocentric ↔ allocentric transformations).
Evaluate multiple LLMs and VLMs (with visual input disabled) on these tasks to compare behavioral performance and failure modes.
Apply interpretability tools — attention-head analysis, neuron attribution/ablation, and causal tracing — to identify internal circuits encoding rotation and positional transformations.
impact: Provides evidence that linguistic priors alone can support key aspects of spatial reasoning and reveals model components responsible for viewpoint transformations; this guides multimodal model design, dataset creation, and targeted interventions for improving spatial generalization.
visual_elements: Example pipeline: textual scene description → rotation query → model output (before/after) with correct/incorrect annotations.
Bar chart comparing task accuracy of LLMs vs VLMs (vision disabled) across rotation difficulty levels.
Attention-head heatmaps / neuron activation maps highlighting components correlated with rotation transformations.
Flowchart of interpretability workflow: probe design → prediction analysis → attribution → targeted ablation and causal test.
paper_title: How Do LLMs and VLMs Understand Viewpoint Rotation Without Vision? An Interpretability Study
paper_authors: Zhen Yang, Ping Jian, Zhongbin Guo, Zuming Zhang, Chengzhi Li
